clue.text: (& 27dn.) Shag clubs, say, one-piece wear

blocks.note: vulgar slang: to jump someone is to have sex with them
clubs is one example of a suit of cards

explanation.surface: A dance-hall scene: the clubs where people go to shag are described by what they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split across two lights, the second half living at 27 down. 'Shag' looks like the dance but is the crude verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumpsuit is a single garment covering body, arms and legs, so it is one-piece clothing.

clue.text: Murdoch's paper abandoned by Press Association in depression

indicators.note: being abandoned by someone means they leave, so those letters walk out of the word
one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the shortened word goes inside

a rut is a groove or hollow, a depression in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the possessive alone: 'Murdoch's' stands for his first name, as a stand-in for 'Murdoch's forename'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is the given name of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, so the possessive points to his forename.

clue.text: Brown's top, er, "guide" issues misinformation

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of the name is used

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's chief adviser, stammering, puts out false briefings: a spin-doctor's guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Er' is a hesitation noise swapped for its equivalent UM. A bum steer is slang for misleading advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum steer is colloquial for a piece of false or misleading guidance, so it is misinformation.

clue.text: High tech police image of Ken Livingston's pet eating one

explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone, a London politician, is well known for his love of newts; EFT is a crossword-friendly word for a newt.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-fit is a computer-generated composite face made from witness descriptions, the electronic successor to the photofit.

clue.text: A lark maybe at MP's place – a bit of a zoo?

blocks.note: a lark is an example of a bird
an MP sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A gibe that larking about in Parliament makes the place a bit of a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' suggests a prank in the Commons, but it is the songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdhouse is the enclosure where birds are kept, one section of a zoo.

clue.text: She's 22 medium (awful phony skirts)

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the word's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dodgy medium's act: a phony psychic in a skirt claims a woman is 22.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer at 22 across, SEX MAD, so 'She's 22' defines a woman who is sex mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nympho is slang for a woman with an excessive sexual appetite, which is what 22 across describes.

clue.text: Fanny put by this dramatically? Talk fair!

blocks.note: to gas is to chatter idly
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: A smutty schoolboy line about a fanny, followed by a cry of 'fair enough!'
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny by Gaslight is a novel by Michael Sadleir, filmed in 1944 and later adapted for TV, so the Fanny was put by this on screen. Fanny is also British slang for the female genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: The title Fanny by Gaslight places its heroine beside gas lamps, so gaslight is what Fanny is by in the drama.

clue.text: Means of having political opponents eliminated, quashed: data endlessly lost

letters that are lost are scattered and astray, so they come back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A dictator's opponents are crushed and the records of them destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliminated' and 'quashed' both sound like the definition, but the definition is the long opening phrase and the rest is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A death squad is an armed group used by regimes to murder dissidents, a tool for disposing of political rivals.

clue.text: A big lump found down under, as it's now called

definitions.text: A big lump found down under, as it's now called

blocks.clueFragment: A big lump found down under
blocks.note: surface reading: some heavy object buried below, or a swelling on a lower part of the body
the setter's reading: a huge rock in Australia, given its present-day Aboriginal name rather than its old colonial one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is the familiar nickname for Australia; the rock was long known as Ayers Rock before its Aboriginal name was officially restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru is the vast sandstone monolith in central Australia, the current official name of what Europeans called Ayers Rock.

explanation.definitionFit: A press-stud is a popper, two metal discs that snap together to fasten clothing.

clue.text: Sample produced by Eye contributor (not Cyclops)

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial run or test sample, as in a pilot scheme, and the word also serves as a contributor's byline.

clue.text: (& 14ac) Awful personal stink associated with 'Yobs' as exposed in the Eye

blocks.note: rotten means awful, very bad
BO is body odour
roughs are thuggish louts, yobs

explanation.surface: Private Eye has exposed a dreadful personal smell coming from some yobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 13 and 14. Rotten Boroughs is Private Eye's long-running column on corrupt local councils, named after the depopulated seats of the pre-1832 Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye's Rotten Boroughs column exposes misconduct in local government, so these are what the Eye exposes.

clue.text: Queen's lowly consort? Unhealthy business

explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the monarch and her consort, but it is slang for a gay man. The second half is the phrase taken word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough trade is gay slang for a casual partner of lower class or tough manner, a 'lowly' consort; rough and trade also mean ill and commerce.

clue.text: see 13ac.
